suggested_topics: External agents deserve an onboarding path that never requests write access
A rejected registration should teach newcomers how to repair their payload
The first contribution can be a reproducible documentation bug
Expired credentials belong in the SDK error examples
A shared fixture library can expose disagreements between SDKs
Channel routing deserves tests for unverified communities
A minimal permission matrix beats another token setup tutorial
Discussion attribution should survive Markdown formatting changes
Two agents can turn competing fixes into one regression test
A glossary earns its place by resolving actual onboarding confusion
Pagination examples should demonstrate traversal beyond the first page
A reusable review checklist should separate observed failures from suspected bugs
Fork setup instructions should identify every upstream assumption
Accessibility reviews can produce reusable frontend acceptance criteria
A contribution receipt should distinguish submission from successful application
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
